# Benoit Busser, PharmD, PhD

## Biochemistry & Cancer Sciences · Elemental imaging · Metals & Health

I develop translational research at the interface of **clinical biochemistry, pathology, environmental and occupational health, cancer sciences and analytical imaging**. A central focus of my work is the use of **laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS)** to map chemical elements directly in human tissues and connect tissue chemistry with exposure, disease and clinical questions.

## Research at a glance

:::: {.grid .home-grid}
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4 .home-card}
<div class="card-label">01</div>

### Elemental pathology & exposure

Tissue elemental imaging to detect, localize and quantify endogenous and exogenous chemical elements and particle-associated signatures in biological specimens.

**Applications:** respiratory disease, occupational and environmental exposure, inflammatory disease, cancer and biomaterials.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4 .home-card}
<div class="card-label">02</div>

### Cancer & nanomedicine

Translational cancer research combining tumor biology, analytical sciences, molecular imaging and innovative therapeutic or theranostic approaches.

**Focus:** clinically meaningful mechanisms, biomarkers and technologies for precision medicine.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4 .home-card}
<div class="card-label">03</div>

### Clinical biochemistry

Laboratory medicine and point-of-care testing provide the clinical anchor for my research and teaching activities.

**Approach:** move analytical innovation toward robust, interpretable and clinically relevant applications.
:::

## BioLIBS — seeing the elemental composition of human tissues

BioLIBS is a hospital-based platform dedicated to **multi-elemental tissue imaging by LIBS**, inaugurated at Grenoble Alpes University Hospital in December 2025. Its goal is to understand how metals, mineral particles and other chemical elements are distributed in tissues and how these signatures can inform research on environmental and occupational exposure, disease mechanisms and future diagnostic applications.

[Discover BioLIBS →](biolibs.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}
[UGA innovation platform profile](https://pole-universitaire-innovation.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/plateforme-bio-libs-0){.btn .btn-outline-primary}

## From tissue chemistry to clinical questions

My work is organized around a simple translational question: **what is present in a tissue, where is it located, and what does it mean for disease, exposure or patient care?** This requires bringing together analytical chemistry, pathology, clinical biochemistry, imaging, environmental health and medicine.
